sanskrit: śrutvā tu param ānandaṃ bharataḥ satyavikramaḥ hṛṣṭam ājñāpayām āsa śatrughnaṃ paravīrahā
english: Hearing the supreme joy, Bharata of true valor, filled with delight, commanded Śatrughna, the slayer of enemy heroes.

sanskrit: daivatāni ca sarvāṇi caityāni nagarasya ca sugandhamālyair vāditrair arcantu śucayo narāḥ
english: "Let all the deities and the sacred shrines of the city be worshipped with fragrant garlands and musical instruments by pure men."

sanskrit: rājadārās tathāmātyāḥ sainyāḥ senāgaṇāṅganāḥ abhiniryāntu rāmasya draṣṭuṃ śaśinibhaṃ mukham
english: "Let the royal ladies, the ministers, the soldiers and the women of the army companies go forth to behold Rāma's face, which resembles the moon."

sanskrit: bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā śatrughnaḥ paravīrahā viṣṭīr anekasāhasrīś codayām āsa vīryavān
english: Hearing Bharata's words, the mighty Śatrughna, slayer of enemy heroes, dispatched many thousands of laborers.

sanskrit: samīkuruta nimnāni viṣamāṇi samāni ca sthānāni ca nirasyantāṃ nandigrāmād itaḥ param
english: "Level the low places and the uneven ground; clear away the obstacles on the road beyond Nandigrāma."

sanskrit: siñcantu pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ himaśītena vāriṇā tato 'bhyavakiraṃs tv anye lājaiḥ puṣpaiś ca sarvataḥ
english: "Sprinkle the entire earth with water cool as snow." Then others scattered parched grain and flowers on all sides.

sanskrit: samucchritapatākās tu rathyāḥ puravarottame śobhayantu ca veśmāni sūryasyodayanaṃ prati
english: "Let the streets of this finest city be adorned with raised banners, and let the dwellings be decorated before the rising of the sun."

sanskrit: sragdāmamuktapuṣpaiś ca sugandhaiḥ pañcavarṇakaiḥ rājamārgam asaṃbādhaṃ kirantu śataśo narāḥ
english: "Let hundreds of men strew the royal road, unobstructed, with garlands and loose flowers of five colors and sweet fragrances."

sanskrit: mattair nāgasahasraiś ca śātakumbhavibhūṣitaḥ apare hemakakṣyābhiḥ sagajābhiḥ kareṇubhiḥ niryayus tvarayā yuktā rathaiś ca sumahārathāḥ
english: With thousands of rutting elephants adorned with gold ornaments, and with female elephants in golden girths, and with great chariot-warriors in chariots, they went forth in swift haste.

sanskrit: tato yānāny upārūḍhāḥ sarvā daśarathastriyaḥ kausalyāṃ pramukhe kṛtvā sumitrāṃ cāpi niryayuḥ
english: Then all the wives of Daśaratha mounted their vehicles and, placing Kausalyā and Sumitrā at the fore, went forth.

sanskrit: aśvānāṃ khuraśabdena rathanemisvanena ca śaṅkhadundubhinādena saṃcacāleva medinī
english: With the sound of the horses' hooves, the rumble of chariot wheels, and the blare of conches and kettledrums, the earth seemed to tremble.

sanskrit: kṛtsnaṃ ca nagaraṃ tat tu nandigrāmam upāgamat dvijātimukhyair dharmātmā śreṇīmukhyaiḥ sanaigamaiḥ
english: The entire city came to Nandigrāma: the pious Bharata, along with the foremost brāhmaṇas, the heads of guilds, and the merchant-leaders.

sanskrit: mālyamodaka hastaiś ca mantribhir bharato vṛtaḥ śaṅkhabherīninādaiś ca bandibhiś cābhivanditaḥ
english: Bharata, surrounded by ministers holding garlands and sweets in their hands, was honored with the sounds of conches and kettledrums and the praises of the bards.

sanskrit: āryapādau gṛhītvā tu śirasā dharmakovidaḥ pāṇḍuraṃ chatram ādāya śuklamālyopaśobhitam
english: That knower of righteousness, having taken up the sandals of his noble elder brother upon his head, bore the white parasol adorned with white garlands,

sanskrit: śukle ca vālavyajane rājārhe hemabhūṣite upavāsakṛśo dīnaś cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaraḥ
english: and the two white yak-tail fans worthy of a king, ornamented with gold — Bharata himself emaciated from fasting, wretched, clad in bark and black antelope skin.

sanskrit: bhrātur āgamanaṃ śrutvā tat pūrvaṃ harṣam āgataḥ pratyudyayau tadā rāmaṃ mahātmā sacivaiḥ saha
english: Having heard of his brother's return, and overcome with prior joy, the great-souled Bharata then went forward to meet Rāma, together with his ministers.

sanskrit: samīkṣya bharato vākyam uvāca pavanātmajam kaccin na khalu kāpeyī sevyate calacittatā na hi paśyāmi kākutsthaṃ rāmam āryaṃ paraṃtapam
english: Gazing about, Bharata spoke to the son of the wind: "Surely the fickleness of the monkey race has not prevailed? For I do not yet see noble Rāma of Kākutstha's line, the scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: athaivam ukte vacane hanūmān idam abravīt arthaṃ vijñāpayann eva bharataṃ satyavikramam
english: When these words had been spoken, Hanūmān said the following, imparting the news to the truly valorous Bharata:

sanskrit: sadā phalān kusumitān vṛkṣān prāpya madhusravān bharadvājaprasādena mattabhramaranāditān
english: "By the grace of Bharadvāja, he has reached trees always laden with fruit and flowers, honey-dripping, resounding with intoxicated bees —

sanskrit: tasya caiṣa varo datto vāsavena paraṃtapa sasainyasya tadātithyaṃ kṛtaṃ sarvaguṇānvitam
english: O scorcher of foes, and this boon was granted by Vāsava himself: hospitality was extended to him together with his army, complete in every virtue.

sanskrit: nisvanaḥ śrūyate bhīmaḥ prahṛṣṭānāṃ vanaukasām manye vānarasenā sā nadīṃ tarati gomatīm
english: A great clamor is heard from the exultant forest-dwellers; I think that monkey army is crossing the river Gomatī.

sanskrit: rajovarṣaṃ samudbhūtaṃ paśya vālukinīṃ prati manye sālavanaṃ ramyaṃ lolayanti plavaṃgamāḥ
english: See the shower of dust arising toward the sandy riverbank; I think the leapers are shaking the pleasant grove of sāla trees.

sanskrit: tad etad dṛśyate dūrād vimalaṃ candrasaṃnibham vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ divyaṃ manasā brahmanirmitam
english: That which is seen in the distance, pure and resembling the moon — that is the divine Puṣpaka aerial car, created by Brahmā through the power of his mind.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ bāndhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ hatvā labdhaṃ mahātmanā dhanadasya prasādena divyam etan manojavam
english: After slaying Rāvaṇa along with his kinsmen, this divine, mind-swift vehicle was obtained by the great-souled one by the favor of Kubera, the lord of wealth.

sanskrit: etasmin bhrātarau vīrau vaidehyā saha rāghavau sugrīvaś ca mahātejā rākṣasendro vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: In it are those two heroic brothers of the Rāghu line together with Vaidehī, and the great-splendored Sugrīva, and Vibhīṣaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tato harṣasamudbhūto nisvano divam aspṛśat strībālayuvavṛddhānāṃ rāmo 'yam iti kīrtitaḥ
english: Then a joyful clamor, arising from women, children, youths and elders alike, rose up to heaven: "This is Rāma!" they proclaimed.

sanskrit: rathakuñjaravājibhyas te 'vatīrya mahīṃ gatāḥ dadṛśus taṃ vimānasthaṃ narāḥ somam ivāmbare
english: Descending from chariots, elephants, and horses and reaching the ground, those men beheld him standing in the aerial car, like the moon in the sky.

sanskrit: prāñjalir bharato bhūtvā prahṛṣṭo rāghavonmukhaḥ svāgatena yathārthena tato rāmam apūjayat
english: Bharata, with joined palms, filled with joy, his face turned toward Rāghava, then honored Rāma with a welcome that was wholly fitting.

sanskrit: manasā brahmaṇā sṛṣṭe vimāne lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ rarāja pṛthudīrghākṣo vajrapāṇir ivāparaḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa's elder brother, with his broad and long eyes, shone in the aerial car created by Brahmā's mind, like a second Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tato vimānagragataṃ bharato bhrātaraṃ tadā vavande praṇato rāmaṃ merustham iva bhāskaram
english: Then Bharata, bowing down, reverenced his brother Rāma positioned at the summit of the aerial car, as one would revere the sun standing upon Mount Meru.

sanskrit: āropito vimānaṃ tad bharataḥ satyavikramaḥ rāmam āsādya muditaḥ punar evābhyavādayat
english: Lifted up into the aerial car, the truly valorous Bharata, having reached Rāma, joyfully saluted him once again.

sanskrit: taṃ samutthāpya kākutsthaḥ cirasyākṣipathaṃ gatam aṅke bharatam āropya muditaḥ pariṣaṣvaje
english: Raising him up, the descendant of Kākutstha, delighted, placed on his lap Bharata, who had for so long been out of sight, and embraced him.

sanskrit: tato lakṣmaṇam āsādya vaidehīṃ ca paraṃtapaḥ abhyavādayata prīto bharato nāma cābravīt
english: Then the scorcher of foes Bharata, going to Lakṣmaṇa and to Vaidehī, saluted them with affection and addressed them by name.

sanskrit: sugrīvaṃ kaikayī putro jāmbavantaṃ tathāṅgadam maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ nīlam ṛṣabhaṃ caiva sasvaje
english: The son of Kaikeyī embraced Sugrīva, Jāmbavān, and Aṅgada, and Mainda, Dvivida, Nīla, and Ṛṣabha as well.

sanskrit: te kṛtvā mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ kuśalaṃ paryapṛcchanta prahṛṣṭā bharataṃ tadā
english: Those shape-shifting monkeys, taking on human form, joyfully enquired after Bharata's well-being.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇaṃ ca bharataḥ sāntvayan vākyam abravīt diṣṭyā tvayā sahāyena kṛtaṃ karma suduṣkaram
english: Reassuring Vibhīṣaṇa, Bharata spoke: "By good fortune was this extremely difficult deed accomplished with you as ally."

sanskrit: śatrughnaś ca tadā rāmam abhivādya salakṣmaṇam sītāyāś caraṇau paścād vavande vinayānvitaḥ
english: Then Śatrughna, saluting Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, afterward reverenced the feet of Sītā with great humility.

sanskrit: rāmo mātaram āsādya viṣaṇṇaṃ śokakarśitām jagrāha praṇataḥ pādau mano mātuś ca prasādayan
english: Rāma, approaching his mother, who was dejected and wasted by grief, bowed and clasped her feet, gladdening her heart.

sanskrit: abhivādya sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ ca yaśasvinīm sa mātṝś ca tadā sarvāḥ purohitam upāgamat
english: Having saluted Sumitrā, the illustrious Kaikeyī, and all his mothers, he then went to the family priest.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ te mahābāho kausalyānandavardhana iti prāñjalayaḥ sarve nāgarā rāmam abruvan
english: "Welcome to you, O mighty-armed one, increaser of Kausalyā's joy" — thus all the townspeople, with joined palms, said to Rāma.

sanskrit: tany añjalisahasrāṇi pragṛhītāni nāgaraiḥ ākośānīva padmāni dadarśa bharatāgrajaḥ
english: Those thousands of joined palms upraised by the townspeople were beheld by Bharata's elder brother like lotuses that had opened their buds.

sanskrit: pāduke te tu rāmasya gṛhītvā bharataḥ svayam caraṇābhyāṃ narendrasya yojayām āsa dharmavit
english: Then Bharata himself, the knower of righteousness, taking Rāma's sandals, placed them upon the feet of that lord of men.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā rāmaṃ bharataḥ sa kṛtāñjaliḥ etat te rakṣitaṃ rājan rājyaṃ niryātitaṃ mayā
english: Then Bharata, with joined palms, said to Rāma: "O king, this kingdom, which was entrusted to me, I now return to you."

sanskrit: adya janma kṛtārthaṃ me saṃvṛttaś ca manorathaḥ yas tvāṃ paśyāmi rājānam ayodhyāṃ punar āgatam
english: "Today my birth is fulfilled and my heart's desire accomplished, in that I behold you, my king, returned to Ayodhyā once more."

sanskrit: avekṣatāṃ bhavān kośaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ puraṃ balam bhavatas tejasā sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ daśaguṇaṃ mayā
english: "May you review the treasury, the granaries, the city, and the army — everything has been increased tenfold by your glory through me."

sanskrit: tathā bruvāṇaṃ bharataṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ bhrātṛvatsalam mumucur vānarā bāṣpaṃ rākṣasaś ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Seeing Bharata speaking thus, so devoted to his brother, the monkeys shed tears, as did the Rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ praharṣād bharatam aṅkam āropya rāghavaḥ yayau tena vimānena sasainyo bharatāśramam
english: Then, in great joy, Rāghava placed Bharata upon his lap and proceeded with that aerial car, along with his army, to Bharata's hermitage.

sanskrit: bharatāśramam āsādya sasainyo rāghavas tadā avatīrya vimānāgrād avatasthe mahītale
english: Having reached Bharata's hermitage, Rāghava then, together with his army, descended from the summit of the aerial car and stood upon the earth.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā rāmas tadvimānam anuttamam vaha vaiśravaṇaṃ devam anujānāmi gamyatām
english: Then Rāma addressed that peerless aerial car: "Carry the god Vaiśravaṇa. I give you leave — depart."

sanskrit: tato rāmābhyanujñātaṃ tadvimānam anuttamam uttarāṃ diśam uddiśya jagāma dhanadālayam
english: Then that peerless aerial car, dismissed by Rāma, went toward the northern quarter, to the home of Kubera, the lord of wealth.

sanskrit: purohitasyātmasamasya rāghavo bṛhaspateḥ śakra ivāmarādhipaḥ nipīḍya pādau pṛthag āsane śubhe sahaiva tenopaviveśa vīryavān
english: The mighty Rāghava, like Indra the lord of the immortals with Bṛhaspati, pressed the feet of the family priest who was equal to his own self, and then sat down together with him on an auspicious seat.

sanskrit: śirasy añjalim ādāya kaikeyīnandivardhanaḥ babhāṣe bharato jyeṣṭhaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam
english: Placing his joined palms upon his head, Bharata, the increaser of Kaikeyī's joy, addressed his elder brother Rāma of true valor:

sanskrit: pūjitā māmikā mātā dattaṃ rājyam idaṃ mama tad dadāmi punas tubhyaṃ yathā tvam adadā mama
english: "My mother was honored, and this kingdom was given to me; I now restore it to you just as you placed it in my hands."

sanskrit: dhuram ekākinā nyastām ṛṣabheṇa balīyasā kiśoravad guruṃ bhāraṃ na voḍhum aham utsahe
english: "The yoke laid down by a single mighty bull — I, like a young calf, am not able to bear this heavy burden."

sanskrit: vārivegena mahatā bhinnaḥ setur iva kṣaran durbandhanam idaṃ manye rājyacchidram asaṃvṛtam
english: "Like a dam broken by the great force of water and leaking, I consider this breach in the kingdom, left unclosed, difficult to stop."

sanskrit: gatiṃ khara ivāśvasya haṃsasyeva ca vāyasaḥ nānvetum utsahe deva tava mārgam ariṃdama
english: "As a donkey cannot follow the gait of a horse, nor a crow that of a goose, so I, O lord, O subduer of enemies, am not able to follow your path."

sanskrit: yathā ca ropito vṛkṣo jātaś cāntarniveśane mahāṃś ca sudurāroho mahāskandhaḥ praśākhavān
english: "Just as a tree planted and grown within a courtyard becomes great, very difficult to climb, with a massive trunk and spreading branches —

sanskrit: śīryeta puṣpito bhūtvā na phalāni pradarśayet tasya nānubhaved arthaṃ yasya hetoḥ sa ropyate
english: "— if it withers after flowering without displaying its fruits, then the purpose of the one for whose sake it was planted is not fulfilled:

sanskrit: eṣopamā mahābāho tvam arthaṃ vettum arhasi yady asmān manujendra tvaṃ bhaktān bhṛtyān na śādhi hi
english: "This is the analogy, O mighty-armed one; you should understand its meaning. O lord of men, if you do not govern us, your devoted servants, the purpose fails."

sanskrit: jagad adyābhiṣiktaṃ tvām anupaśyatu sarvataḥ pratapantam ivādityaṃ madhyāhne dīptatejasaṃ
english: "Let the world today behold you, anointed king, resplendent on all sides like the sun blazing at midday with brilliant light."

sanskrit: tūryasaṃghātanirghoṣaiḥ kāñcīnūpuranisvanaiḥ madhurair gītaśabdaiś ca pratibudhyasva śeṣva ca
english: "May you awake and sleep to the combined sounds of musical instruments, to the jingling of girdles and anklets, and to the sweet sounds of song."

sanskrit: yāvad āvartate cakraṃ yāvatī ca vasuṃdharā tāvat tvam iha sarvasya svāmitvam abhivartaya
english: "For as long as the wheel of time turns, and for as long as this earth endures, so long may you exercise here lordship over all."

sanskrit: bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ tatheti pratijagrāha niṣasādāsane śubhe
english: Hearing Bharata's words, Rāma, the conqueror of enemy cities, accepted with "So be it" and sat down on the auspicious seat.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatrughnavacanān nipuṇāḥ śmaśruvardhakāḥ sukhahastāḥ suśīghrāś ca rāghavaṃ paryupāsata
english: Then, at Śatrughna's command, skilled barbers with gentle hands, swift and deft, attended upon Rāghava.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ tu bharate snāte lakṣmaṇe ca mahābale sugrīve vānarendre ca rākṣasendre vibhīṣaṇe
english: First Bharata bathed, then the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, then Sugrīva the lord of monkeys, and then Vibhīṣaṇa the lord of Rākṣasas —

sanskrit: viśodhitajaṭaḥ snātaś citramālyānulepanaḥ mahārhavasanopetas tasthau tatra śriyā jvalan
english: Rāma, with his matted locks removed, bathed, anointed with colorful garlands, adorned with the most excellent garments, stood there blazing with royal glory.

sanskrit: pratikarma ca rāmasya kārayām āsa vīryavān lakṣmaṇasya ca lakṣmīvān ikṣvākukulavardhanaḥ
english: The glorious increaser of the Ikṣvāku line caused the adornment of Rāma, and also of Lakṣmaṇa, to be performed by the mighty.

sanskrit: pratikarma ca sītāyāḥ sarvā daśarathastriyaḥ ātmanaiva tadā cakrur manasvinyo manoharam
english: And the adornment of Sītā was carried out by all the wives of Daśaratha themselves, those high-minded women making it charming.

sanskrit: tato rāghavapatnīnāṃ sarvāsām eva śobhanam cakāra yatnāt kausalyā prahṛṣṭā putravatsalā
english: Then the joyful Kausalyā, devoted to her son, took pains to adorn beautifully all the wives of Rāghava.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatrughnavacanāt sumantro nāma sārathiḥ yojayitvābhicakrāma rathaṃ sarvāṅgaśobhanam
english: Then, at Śatrughna's command, the charioteer named Sumantra, having yoked the horses, brought forward a chariot beautiful in all its parts.

sanskrit: arkamaṇḍalasaṃkāśaṃ divyaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathaṃ sthitam āruroha mahābāhū rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
english: Seeing the divine chariot standing there, resembling the orb of the sun, the mighty-armed Rāma of true valor mounted it.

sanskrit: ayodhyāyāṃ tu sacivā rājño daśarathasya ye purohitaṃ puraskṛtya mantrayām āsur arthavat
english: The ministers of King Daśaratha who were in Ayodhyā, placing the family priest at their head, took counsel purposefully:

sanskrit: mantrayan rāmavṛddhyarthaṃ vṛttyarthaṃ nagarasya ca sarvam evābhiṣekārthaṃ jayārhasya mahātmanaḥ kartum arhatha rāmasya yad yan maṅgalapūrvakam
english: "Deliberating for the prosperity of Rāma and for the welfare of the city, everything for the sake of the coronation — you should perform for the great-souled Rāma, who deserves victory, whatever is auspicious, preceded by sacred rites."

sanskrit: iti te mantriṇaḥ sarve saṃdiśya tu purohitam nagarān niryayus tūrṇaṃ rāmadarśanabuddhayaḥ
english: Thus all those ministers, having instructed the family priest, quickly went forth from the city with the intention of seeing Rāma.

sanskrit: hariyuktaṃ sahasrākṣo ratham indra ivānaghaḥ prayayau ratham āsthāya rāmo nagaram uttamam
english: Like the thousand-eyed Indra seated in a horse-drawn chariot — sinless Rāma, ascending the chariot, set out for the royal city.

sanskrit: jagrāha bharato raśmīñ śatrughnaś chatram ādade lakṣmaṇo vyajanaṃ tasya mūrdhni saṃparyavījayat
english: Bharata took the reins; Śatrughna held the parasol; Lakṣmaṇa fanned him from above with a fan over his head.

sanskrit: śvetaṃ ca vālavyajanaṃ sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ aparaṃ candrasaṃkāśaṃ rākṣasendro vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: And the white yak-tail fan was held by Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys; the other, resembling the moon, was held by Vibhīṣaṇa, the lord of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: ṛṣisaṃghair tadākāśe devaiś ca samarudgaṇaiḥ stūyamānasya rāmasya śuśruve madhuradhvaniḥ
english: As Rāma was being praised by assemblies of sages in the sky, and by the gods together with the Marut hosts, a sweet sound was heard.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatruṃjayaṃ nāma kuñjaraṃ parvatopamam āruroha mahātejāḥ sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ
english: Then the greatly splendored Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, mounted an elephant named Śatruṃjaya, which was mountain-like in size.

sanskrit: navanāgasahasrāṇi yayur āsthāya vānarāḥ mānuṣaṃ vigrahaṃ kṛtvā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
english: Nine thousand elephants set out, mounted by monkeys who had taken on human form, adorned with all manner of ornaments.

sanskrit: śaṅkhaśabdapraṇādaiś ca dundubhīnāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ prayayū puruṣavyāghras tāṃ purīṃ harmyamālinīm
english: To the resounding blasts of conches and the beating of kettledrums, that tiger among men proceeded to that city garlanded with mansions.

sanskrit: dadṛśus te samāyāntaṃ rāghavaṃ sapuraḥsaram virājamānaṃ vapuṣā rathenātirathaṃ tadā
english: They then saw Rāghava coming with his vanguard, shining in his form upon the chariot — that greatest of chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: te vardhayitvā kākutsthaṃ rāmeṇa pratinanditāḥ anujagmur mahātmānaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritam
english: They, having acclaimed the descendant of Kākutstha and been welcomed in return by Rāma, followed the great-souled one who was surrounded by his brothers.

sanskrit: amātyair brāhmaṇaiś caiva tathā prakṛtibhir vṛtaḥ śriyā viruruce rāmo nakṣatrair iva candramāḥ
english: Surrounded by ministers, brāhmaṇas, and the people, Rāma shone with royal glory like the moon among the stars.

sanskrit: sa purogāmibhis tūryais tālasvastikapāṇibhiḥ pravyāharadbhir muditair maṅgalāni yayau vṛtaḥ
english: He went forth accompanied by the vanguard musicians, by joyful attendants bearing tāla-palms and auspicious svastika emblems, who proclaimed blessings.

sanskrit: akṣataṃ jātarūpaṃ ca gāvaḥ kanyās tathā dvijāḥ narā modakahastāś ca rāmasya purato yayuḥ
english: Unbroken grain, gold, cows, maidens, brāhmaṇas, and men bearing sweet cakes went ahead of Rāma.

sanskrit: sakhyaṃ ca rāmaḥ sugrīve prabhāvaṃ cānilātmaje vānarāṇāṃ ca tat karma vyācacakṣe 'tha mantriṇām śrutvā ca vismayaṃ jagmur ayodhyāpuravāsinaḥ
english: Then Rāma recounted to the ministers his friendship with Sugrīva, the might of the son of the wind, and the deeds of the monkeys; the inhabitants of the city of Ayodhyā, hearing this, were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: dyutimān etad ākhyāya rāmo vānarasaṃvṛtaḥ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇām ayodhyāṃ praviveśa ha
english: The resplendent Rāma, having thus narrated this, surrounded by the monkeys, entered Ayodhyā, which was thronged with joyful and prosperous people.

sanskrit: tato hy abhyucchrayan paurāḥ patākās te gṛhe gṛhe aikṣvākādhyuṣitaṃ ramyam āsasāda pitur gṛham
english: Then the citizens raised flags on each and every house, and he reached the beautiful paternal home of the Ikṣvāku dynasty.

sanskrit: pitur bhavanam āsādya praviśya ca mahātmanaḥ kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ cābhyavādayat
english: Reaching and entering the dwelling of his great-souled father, he saluted Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: athābravīd rājaputro bharataṃ dharmiṇāṃ varam athopahitayā vācā madhuraṃ raghunandanaḥ
english: Then the prince, the joy of the Raghu line, spoke to Bharata, the best among the righteous, with a well-measured, sweet voice:

sanskrit: yac ca madbhavanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sāśokavanikaṃ mahat muktāvaidūryasaṃkīrṇaṃ sugrīvasya nivedaya
english: "Show to Sugrīva my finest dwelling, with its great grove of aśoka trees, interspersed with pearls and vaidūrya gems."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā bharataḥ satyavikramaḥ pāṇau gṛhītvā sugrīvaṃ praviveśa tam ālayam
english: Hearing those words, the truly valorous Bharata, taking Sugrīva by the hand, entered that dwelling.

sanskrit: tatas tailapradīpāṃś ca paryaṅkāstaraṇāni ca gṛhītvā viviśuḥ kṣipraṃ śatrughnena pracoditāḥ
english: Then, prompted by Śatrughna, they quickly entered, bringing oil lamps and fine coverlets for couches.

sanskrit: uvāca ca mahātejāḥ sugrīvaṃ rāghavānujaḥ abhiṣekāya rāmasya dūtān ājñāpaya prabho
english: And the greatly splendored younger brother of Rāghava said to Sugrīva: "O lord, dispatch messengers for the coronation of Rāma."

sanskrit: sauvarṇān vānarendrāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ caturo ghaṭān dadau kṣipraṃ sa sugrīvaḥ sarvaratnavibhūṣitān
english: Sugrīva quickly gave four golden jars to four lords among the monkeys, adorned with all kinds of jewels.

sanskrit: yathā pratyūṣasamaye caturṇāṃ sāgarāmbhasām pūrṇair ghaṭaiḥ pratīkṣadhvaṃ tathā kuruta vānarāḥ
english: "At the hour of dawn, wait with jars filled with the waters of the four oceans — do it thus, O monkeys."

sanskrit: evam uktā mahātmāno vānarā vāraṇopamāḥ utpetur gaganaṃ śīghraṃ garuḍā iva śīghragāḥ
english: Thus addressed, those great-souled monkeys, elephant-like in strength, leapt swiftly into the sky like fast-flying Garuḍas.

sanskrit: jāmbavāṃś ca hanūmāṃś ca vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ ṛṣabhaś caiva kalaśāñ jalapūrṇān athānayan nadīśatānāṃ pañcānāṃ jale kumbhair upāharan
english: Jāmbavān, Hanūmān, the monkey Vegadarśī, and Ṛṣabha brought back water-filled jars; with pots they brought the waters of five hundred rivers.

sanskrit: pūrvāt samudrāt kalaśaṃ jalapūrṇam athānayat suṣeṇaḥ sattvasaṃpannaḥ sarvaratnavibhūṣitam
english: The valiant Suṣeṇa brought a water-filled jar from the eastern ocean, adorned with all kinds of jewels.

sanskrit: ṛṣabho dakṣiṇāt tūrṇaṃ samudrāj jalam āharat
english: Ṛṣabha swiftly fetched water from the southern ocean.

sanskrit: raktacandanakarpūraiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ kāñcanaṃ ghaṭam gavayaḥ paścimāt toyam ājahāra mahārṇavāt
english: Gavaya brought a golden jar encased in red sandalwood and camphor, carrying water from the vast western ocean.

sanskrit: ratnakumbhena mahatā śītaṃ mārutavikramaḥ uttarāc ca jalaṃ śīghraṃ garuḍānilavikramaḥ
english: Mārutavikrama, swift as Garuḍa and the wind, quickly fetched cool water from the northern ocean in a great jeweled jar.

sanskrit: abhiṣekāya rāmasya śatrughnaḥ sacivaiḥ saha purohitāya śreṣṭhāya suhṛdbhyaś ca nyavedayat
english: Śatrughna, together with the ministers, presented these for the coronation of Rāma to the foremost family priest and to his friends.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa prayato vṛddho vasiṣṭho brāhmaṇaiḥ saha rāmaṃ ratnamayo pīṭhe sahasītaṃ nyaveśayat
english: Then the venerable Vasiṣṭha, ritually pure, together with the brāhmaṇas, seated Rāma together with Sītā on a jeweled throne.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho vāmadevaś ca jābālir atha kāśyapaḥ kātyāyanaḥ suyajñaś ca gautamo vijayas tathā
english: Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Jābāli, Kāśyapa, Kātyāyana, Suyajña, Gautama, and Vijaya —

sanskrit: abhyaṣiñcan naravyāghraṃ prasannena sugandhinā salilena sahasrākṣaṃ vasavo vāsavaṃ yathā
english: — these consecrated that tiger among men with clear, fragrant water, as the Vasus consecrate the thousand-eyed Indra.

sanskrit: ṛtvigbhir brāhmaṇaiḥ pūrvaṃ kanyābhir mantribhis tathā yodhaiś caivābhyaṣiñcaṃs te saṃprahṛṣṭāḥ sanaigamaiḥ
english: First the officiating priests, then brāhmaṇas, then maidens, ministers, warriors, and merchants, all filled with joy, consecrated him.

sanskrit: sarvauṣadhirasaiś cāpi daivatair nabhasi sthitaiḥ caturhir lokapālaiś ca sarvair devaiś ca saṃgataiḥ
english: With the essences of all medicinal herbs, and also by the gods stationed in the sky, by the four guardians of the world, and by all the gods assembled together.

sanskrit: chatraṃ tasya ca jagrāha śatrughnaḥ pāṇḍuraṃ śubham śvetaṃ ca vālavyajanaṃ sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ aparaṃ candrasaṃkāśaṃ rākṣasendro vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Śatrughna held the pure white, auspicious royal parasol over him; the white yak-tail fan was held by Sugrīva the lord of monkeys; the other, resembling the moon, was held by Vibhīṣaṇa the lord of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: mālāṃ jvalantīṃ vapuṣā kāñcanīṃ śatapuṣkarām rāghavāya dadau vāyur vāsavena pracoditaḥ
english: Vāyu, the wind god, prompted by Vāsava, gave to Rāghava a golden garland of a hundred lotuses blazing with beauty.

sanskrit: sarvaratnasamāyuktaṃ maṇiratnavibhūṣitam muktāhāraṃ narendrāya dadau śakrapracoditaḥ
english: The one prompted by Śakra gave to the lord of men a pearl necklace filled with all kinds of precious stones and adorned with jeweled gems.

sanskrit: prajagur devagandharvā nanṛtuś cāpsaro gaṇāḥ abhiṣeke tad arhasya tadā rāmasya dhīmataḥ
english: The divine Gandharvas sang and hosts of Apsarases danced at the coronation of the wise Rāma, who was worthy of such honor.

sanskrit: bhūmiḥ sasyavatī caiva phalavantaś ca pādapāḥ gandhavanti ca puṣpāṇi babhūvū rāghavotsave
english: The earth brought forth abundant grain, the trees bore fruit, and the flowers became fragrant at the festival of Rāghava's coronation.

sanskrit: sahasraśatam aśvānāṃ dhenūnāṃ ca gavāṃ tathā dadau śataṃ vṛṣān pūrvaṃ dvijebhyo manujarṣabhaḥ
english: That bull among men first gave one hundred thousand horses and one hundred thousand milk cows, and one hundred bulls, to the twice-born.

sanskrit: triṃśatkoṭīr hiraṇyasya brāhmaṇebhyo dadau punaḥ nānābharaṇavastrāṇi mahārhāṇi ca rāghavaḥ
english: Rāghava further gave to the brāhmaṇas thirty crores of gold, and various most excellent ornaments and garments.

sanskrit: arkaraśmipratīkāśāṃ kāñcanīṃ maṇivigrahām sugrīvāya srajaṃ divyāṃ prāyacchan manujarṣabhaḥ
english: That bull among men gave to Sugrīva a divine golden garland set with gems, resembling the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: vaidūryamaṇicitre ca vajraratnavibhūṣite vāliputrāya dhṛtimān aṅgadāyāṅgade dadau
english: The steadfast Rāma gave to Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, golden armlets embellished with vaidūrya gems and adorned with diamond gems.

sanskrit: maṇipravarajuṣṭaṃ ca muktāhāram anuttamam sītāyai pradadau rāmaś candraraśmisamaprabham
english: Rāma gave to Sītā a peerless pearl necklace adorned with the finest gems, brilliant as the rays of the moon.

sanskrit: araje vāsasī divye śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca avekṣamāṇā vaidehī pradadau vāyusūnave
english: Vaidehī, gazing about, gave to the son of the wind god two spotless divine garments and auspicious ornaments.

sanskrit: avamucyātmanaḥ kaṇṭhād dhāraṃ janakanandinī avaikṣata harīn sarvān bhartāraṃ ca muhur muhuḥ
english: The daughter of Janaka, removing a necklace from her own throat, looked again and again at all the monkeys and then at her husband.

sanskrit: tām iṅgitajñaḥ saṃprekṣya babhāṣe janakātmajām pradehi subhage hāraṃ yasya tuṣṭāsi bhāmini
english: Rāma, who understood her gestures, looking at her, said to the daughter of Janaka: "Give the necklace, O beautiful one, to him with whom you are pleased, O passionate lady."

sanskrit: pauruṣaṃ vikramo buddhir yasminn etāni nityadā dadau sā vāyuputrāya taṃ hāram asitekṣaṇā
english: She, the dark-eyed one, gave that necklace to the son of the wind god, in whom such manly virtue, valor, and wisdom are ever present.

sanskrit: hanūmāṃs tena hāreṇa śuśubhe vānararṣabhaḥ candrāṃśucayagaureṇa śvetābhreṇa yathācalaḥ
english: Hanūmān, that bull among monkeys, shone with that necklace, white as the beams of the moon, like a mountain covered with white clouds.

sanskrit: tato dvivida maindābhyāṃ nīlāya ca paraṃtapaḥ sarvān kāmaguṇān vīkṣya pradadau vasudhādhipaḥ
english: Then the scorcher of foes, the lord of the earth, surveying all their merits and desires, gave to Dvivida, Mainda, and Nīla all that they desired.

sanskrit: sarvavānaravṛddhāś ca ye cānye vānareśvarāḥ vāsobhir bhūṣaṇaiś caiva yathārhaṃ pratipūjitāḥ
english: All the elder monkeys and whatever other lords among the monkeys there were — all were honored fittingly with garments and ornaments.

sanskrit: yathārhaṃ pūjitāḥ sarve kāmai ratnaiś ca puṣkalair prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve jagmur eva yathāgatam
english: All of them, honored fittingly with desired gifts and fine jewels, their hearts filled with joy, departed even as they had come.

sanskrit: rāghavaḥ paramodāraḥ śaśāsa parayā mudā uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmo dharmajñaṃ dharmavatsalaḥ
english: The supremely generous Rāghava ruled with great joy; Rāma, devoted to righteousness and knowing righteousness, said to Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: ātiṣṭha dharmajña mayā sahemāṃ gāṃ pūrvarājādhyuṣitāṃ balena tulyaṃ mayā tvaṃ pitṛbhir dhṛtā yā tāṃ yauvarājye dhuram udvahasva
english: "O knower of righteousness, undertake together with me the governance of this earth, which was formerly held by royal ancestors equal in strength to me; bear the burden of the crown prince's office."

sanskrit: sarvātmanā paryanunīyamāno yadā na saumitrir upaiti yogam niyujyamāno bhuvi yauvarājye tato 'bhyaṣiñcad bharataṃ mahātmā
english: When the son of Sumitrā, though entreated with his whole being and though appointed to the crown prince's office on earth, did not accept the role, the great-souled one then consecrated Bharata.

sanskrit: rāghavaś cāpi dharmātmā prāpya rājyam anuttamam īje bahuvidhair yajñaiḥ sasuhṛdbhrātṛbāndhavaḥ
english: And the righteous Rāghava, having attained the incomparable kingdom, performed sacrifices of many kinds together with friends, brothers, and kinsmen.

sanskrit: pauṇḍarīkāśvamedhābhyāṃ vājapeyena cāsakṛt anyaiś ca vividhair yajñair ayajat pārthivarṣabhaḥ
english: That bull among kings sacrificed with the Pauṇḍarīka and the Aśvamedha, repeatedly with the Vājapeya, and with many other various sacrifices.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ daśasahasrāṇi prāpya varṣāṇi rāghavaḥ śatāśvamedhān ājahre sadaśvān bhūridakṣiṇān
english: Having ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years, Rāghava performed a hundred horse-sacrifices with fine horses and great sacrificial gifts.

sanskrit: ājānulambibāhuś ca mahāskandhaḥ pratāpavān lakṣmaṇānucaro rāmaḥ pṛthivīm anvapālayat
english: Rāma, with arms hanging down to his knees, with a mighty chest, resplendent in glory, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, protected the earth.

sanskrit: na paryadevan vidhavā na ca vyālakṛtaṃ bhayam na vyādhijaṃ bhayaṃ vāpi rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
english: No widow lamented, there was no fear caused by serpents, no fear born of disease either, while Rāma was governing the kingdom.

sanskrit: nirdasyur abhaval loko nānarthaḥ kaṃ cid aspṛśat na ca sma vṛddhā bālānāṃ pretakāryāṇi kurvate
english: The world was free of robbers; no misfortune touched anyone; nor did the old perform the funeral rites of the young.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ muditam evāsīt sarvo dharmaparo 'bhavat rāmam evānupaśyanto nābhyahiṃsan parasparam
english: Everything was joyful; everyone was devoted to righteousness; keeping their eyes on Rāma alone, they did not harm one another.

sanskrit: āsan varṣasahasrāṇi tathā putrasahasriṇaḥ nirāmayā viśokāś ca rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
english: People lived for a thousand years and had a thousand sons, free from disease and grief, while Rāma was governing the kingdom.

sanskrit: nityapuṣpā nityaphalās taravaḥ skandhavistṛtāḥ kālavarṣī ca parjanyaḥ sukhasparśaś ca mārutaḥ
english: The trees bore flowers always and fruit always, with wide-spreading trunks; the rain fell in due season; the wind was pleasant to the touch.

sanskrit: svakarmasu pravartante tuṣṭhāḥ svair eva karmabhiḥ āsan prajā dharmaparā rāme śāsati nānṛtāḥ
english: The subjects pursued their own duties, content with their own occupations; the people were devoted to righteousness and were truthful while Rāma ruled.

sanskrit: sarve lakṣaṇasaṃpannāḥ sarve dharmaparāyaṇāḥ daśavarṣasahasrāṇi rāmo rājyam akārayat
english: All were endowed with auspicious marks; all were devoted to righteousness; Rāma caused the kingdom to flourish for ten thousand years.
